## ✨ What's new in 1.1

Cindl 1.1 gives Talk a workspace inspired by T3 Code, with conversations beside
it, finished work folded away and questions kept close to the composer.

- **Conversations in reach.** On web and desktop, a resizable list pins the main
  conversation and shows what needs you, what is working and what finished while
  you were elsewhere. The switcher on phones and Android shows Done, Failed or
  Stopped too, until you open the conversation.
- **A quieter work log.** Finished steps fold into a summary on web, desktop and
  Android. Running and blocked work starts open, and a selected step stays in
  view.
- **Questions above the composer.** On tablets and larger web and desktop
  windows, question sets show one question at a time, with number keys and a fold
  control. Approvals stay beside the work they hold, answered once.
- **Clearer Send and Stop.** One round action changes with what you are doing.
  A rapid second press on Send cannot stop the turn.
- **Faster keyboard work.** Web and desktop add list navigation, in-place
  renaming, previous-message recall and a grouped command palette. Focus follows
  conversations and steps when they move.
- **Smaller details.** Day-aware times, clearer working timers, better phone tabs
  and linked conversations on Work. Web and desktop also add Copy controls and
  folding for long messages.

No Hermes configuration changes or data migrations are needed. Cindl still
connects to your existing `hermes serve`; the pinned API baseline remains
Hermes v0.22.5.

## ⬇️ Install or update

| File                                    | For                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Cindl-1.1.0-x86_64.AppImage`           | Linux x64. Make it executable and run it.                                                                                         |
| `Cindl-Setup-1.1.0.exe`                 | Windows x64. The installer is not code-signed.                                                                                    |
| `cindl-1.1.0-android.apk`               | Android 7.0 or later. Install over the previous release to update it.                                                             |
| `cindl-web-1.1.0.tar`, `cindl-serve.py` | The web client at `/cindl/`. See [Running Cindl](https://github.com/FlintSH/cindl/blob/v1.1.0/docs/handbook/operations/index.md). |

The Android release keeps the same package name and signing key. Its licence
notices and APK check report are in `cindl-1.1.0-android-notices.zip`.

### Verify

`SHA256SUMS` lists every file. The APK is signed with the same certificate as
1.0.0:

```text
SHA-256: A4:10:5F:20:F7:FA:59:01:03:5E:B0:8D:B2:2E:02:CC:84:02:B9:22:F5:9D:77:D7:9E:53:2A:92:0E:2B:B9:B6
```

Check it with `apksigner verify --print-certs cindl-1.1.0-android.apk`.

## ⚠️ Known limits

- The AppImage and Windows installer are not code-signed.
- Without a usable system keyring, the desktop app keeps tokens in memory and
  asks you to sign in again after a restart.
- Some browsers reserve Ctrl/⌘ Shift [ and ] for browser tabs; the desktop app
  can use them to move between conversations.
- CI uses a fake Hermes, an Android emulator and both desktop builds. Physical
  Android and TalkBack checks remain manual; see the
  [acceptance matrix](https://github.com/FlintSH/cindl/blob/v1.1.0/docs/handbook/project/acceptance-matrix.md).
